correctness.rationale: The six triple points and their unique smooth conic are recovered from the unlabelled arrangement. The nine pairwise chords determine the connected K3,3 graph and its unique two-coloring up to interchange, which reconstructs the six-point 3+3 marked branch set. The genus-two even-theta dictionary is explicit in Lange--Ortega Section 3 and (7.1); both constructions are algebraic and PGL-equivariant. Dimension 3, generic degree 10, and stabilizer equivalence follow from the common quotient and genus-two hyperelliptic lift. The embedded exact arithmetic checker exhausts all ten partitions for a rational sextuple and all 120 candidate Möbius symmetries. It is only a nonempty-open witness, not a universal proof. The source theorem supplies rather than independently derives mdr=5.

originality.rationale: The lead work establishes the conic-specific Jacobian jump but not the intrinsic spin marking; Lange--Ortega establishes the classical even-theta partition and quotient but not the unlabelled nine-line reconstruction. Their known results are credited as antecedents. Comparison with older Ziegler moduli and nine-line moduli sources and with eight semantic queries uncovered no explicit or implication-equivalent bridge; an older alternative-terminology treatment is a real residual bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: Classical invariant theory of six points on a conic may describe the same nine chords and bipartition without Ziegler terminology.
Generality/stack statements are restricted to coarse moduli, and no assertion is made for reducible-conic or additional-concurrence boundary.

value.rationale: The syzygy-jump locus of a natural nine-line arrangement family becomes a concrete genus-two even-spin moduli space, with a ten-sheet forgetful structure and a conceptual projective stabilizer formula. The claim classifies an entire motivated positive-dimensional family and its geometric marking, not an arbitrary finite slice or routine table value; it leaves boundary/compactification questions open.
